en: The Eleven-Faced Heart-Dharani Sutra, translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavat was dwelling at the Bamboo Sprout Vihara in Śrāvastī.
He was accompanied by a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
as well as immeasurable and incalculable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
with the Bodhisattva Maitreya as their leader.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas and upāsikās, as well as devas,
nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, kumbhāṇḍas, piśācas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.
Surrounded by a great assembly who made offerings, paid homage, revered,
and praised him, he preached the Dharma for them.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara—
Surrounded before and behind by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of mantra-holding ṛṣis,
he approached the place where the Buddha was;
having arrived, he prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One.
Having circumambulated [the Buddha] three times to the right, he withdrew to sit at one side and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
I possess a heart-mantra named 'Eleven Faces'."
Possessing great majestic power,
it has been spoken by eleven koṭis of Buddhas;
I shall now proclaim it.
For the sake of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings;
for the purpose of eliminating all diseases; for the purpose of extinguishing all evils;
and for the purpose of halting all inauspiciousness.
It is for the purpose of dispelling all evil dreams;
for the purpose of warding off all untimely deaths;
and with the desire to bring those with evil minds to discipline and purity.
It is because those who possess sorrow and suffering obtain peace and happiness;
those who have enemies and adversaries attain reconciliation;
and all demonic obstacles are utterly extinguished.
Because all that the mind desires and seeks is fulfilled accordingly.
World-Honored One, I do not see anyone in the world—whether among the devas, Māras, Brahmās, śramaṇas, or brāhmaṇas—who [can surpass this].
By means of this divine mantra, one shall protect one's body;
by receiving, upholding, reciting, copying, and disseminating it,
one shall be shielded from all calamities, misfortunes, and demonic obstacles.
I do not see anything that can cause harm— such as swords, staves, poisons,
or malevolent incantations and spells— within the boundary established by this divine mantra,
whether it be far or near, wherever one dwells.
There is no one capable of coming to harass or harm them,
except for those whose determinate evil karma is destined to ripen.
World-Honored One, may you bear witness that this matter is necessarily so.
One should only believe and accept it, and not engage in conceptual discrimination.
In this way, all calamities and misfortunes will be entirely kept at a distance and unable to approach.
This heart-mantra of the divine spell is praised and rejoiced in by all Buddhas alike;
it is remembered and protected by all Tathāgatas.
"Bhagavān, I recall that in the past, more than as many eons ago as there are grains of sand in the Ganges,
there appeared in the world a Buddha named Śatapatrākṣa-anāvaraṇa-śikhara-jvalita-guṇaprabha-rāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
At that time, I was a great rishi.
From that World-Honored One, I received this dhāraṇī.
Upon receiving this dhāraṇī, I beheld the Buddhas of the ten directions.
At that time, they shall realize the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
You should know that this mantra possesses great majestic power;
therefore, if there are sons or daughters of good family who possess pure faith, [they should recite it].
Those who wish to receive, uphold, read, and recite this divine mantra should maintain a respectful and sincere mind with focused mindfulness.
Every morning, they should purify themselves according to the Dharma.
Recite this mantra one hundred and eight times.
If one is able to do so,
one will obtain ten kinds of benefits in this very life.
What are these ten?
First, the body is always free from illness.
Second, one is constantly sustained by the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Third, wealth, treasures, clothing, and food will be enjoyed without end.
Fourth, one will be able to subdue enemies and adversaries without fear.
Fifth, all those of noble status will show respect and address one first.
Sixth, they cannot be harmed by malevolent poisons or demonic spirits.
Seventh, they cannot be injured by any blades or weapons.
Eighth, they cannot be drowned by water.
Ninth, fire cannot burn them.
Tenth, they shall never meet with an untimely death.
Furthermore, they shall obtain four kinds of meritorious benefits.
First, at the time of death, one shall behold all the Buddhas;
second, one shall never fall into the various evil realms;
third, one shall not die due to perilous calamities.
Fourth, one will attain birth in the world of Ultimate Bliss.
World-Honored One, I recall that in the past, more than ten *gaṅgā* sands of *kalpas* ago,
and even further back than that, a Buddha appeared in the world.
He was named Surasvaragandha Tathāgata, Arhat,
Samyaksaṃbuddha. At that time, I was a great householder who received this dhāraṇī from that Buddha.
Upon obtaining this mantra, one immediately transcends forty thousand kalpas of birth and death.
By reciting and upholding this mantra,
one further attains the treasury of great compassionate wisdom of all Buddhas and the gates of liberation of all Bodhisattvas.
By this power, one is able to rescue all those imprisoned and confined in jails,
those bound by cangues, shackles, and pillories facing execution, and those afflicted by water,
fire, wind, bandits, malevolent poisons, or curses and incantations.
Regarding the various hardships and calamities caused by humans,
non-humans, and others, through this, I am able to act as a refuge, a protector, a consolation, an island, and a dwelling for all sentient beings.
By the power of this mantra, one shall subdue all malevolent yakṣas, rākṣasas, and others;
first causing them to give rise to a mind of loving-kindness and compassion,
one shall thereafter establish them in anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
"Bhagavān, this divine mantra of mine possesses great power;
if recited even once, it can immediately eliminate the four root transgressions and the five crimes of immediate retribution, leaving nothing remaining."
How much more so for those who are able to practice according to the teaching!
Those who have planted various roots of goodness under hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddhas shall now be able to hear this dhāraṇī.
How much more so for those who can receive, uphold, and practice according to the teaching!
If anyone can read, recite, receive, and uphold this divine mantra day and night,
I shall cause all their aspirations and requests to be fulfilled exactly as they wish.
If there are those who, every half-month—
on either the fourteenth or the fifteenth day—
observe the fast and precepts in accordance with the Dharma and remain pure.
If one fixes the mind upon me and recites this divine mantra,
they will immediately transcend forty thousand kalpas of birth and death.
World-Honored One, by means of this mantra, I—
My name is noble and difficult to hear; yet,
while one might recite the names of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddhas,
there is another who for a brief moment recites my name with a sincere heart.
Those two merits are perfectly equal.
All those who call upon my name shall attain the stage of non-retrogression.
They shall be free from all illnesses, liberated from all obstructions and all fears,
and shall be able to extinguish and eliminate the evils of body, speech, and mind;
how much more so, then, regarding the divine mantra I have spoken.
If one upholds, recites, and practices according to the teaching,
you should know that for such a person, unsurpassed enlightenment will be received as if held in the palm of the hand.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
You are indeed able [to act] toward all sentient beings."
Having generated such a mind of great compassion,
he desires to reveal this great divine mantra.
O son of good family, by means of this skillful method, you [shall attain it].
It is able to rescue and liberate all sentient beings from all sickness,
suffering, obstacles, difficulties, fears, and the evils of body, speech, and mind,
even unto establishing all sentient beings [in the state of peace].
"Regarding this *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, son of good family, I too rejoice; I accept your divine mantra. You should now proclaim it.

Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat, bared one shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, and addressed the Buddha, saying: "Those who recite this mantra should speak as follows."
Homage to the Triple Gem.
Homage to the Tathāgata, the Holy Ocean of Wisdom, the All-Illuminating Adornment King.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Homage to the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One.

Tadyathā: aṃ (1) dara (2) dara (3) diri diri (4) duru duru (5) iḍe vaḍe (6) chele chele (7) prachele prachele (8) kusume (9) kusumavaḍe (10) iri miri (11) ciri ciri (12) śimavare (13) śūṣule mahāsattva (14) mahākāruṇike (15) svāhā. World-Honored One, this is the root mantra.
If one recites this, one shall obtain the meritorious benefits as described above.
Homage to the Triple Gem.
Homage to the Tathāgata Āryajñānasāgaravairocanavyūharāja.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Greatly Compassionate One.
Tadyathā | ha ha ha ha | i li mi li | ci li pi li | ki li hi li | svāhā. World-Honored One, this is the mantra for consecrating water and clothing.
If one wishes to enter the maṇḍala, one should first bathe.
Thereafter, one should empower water with this mantra seven times and sprinkle it upon the body to achieve purification.
Furthermore, one should empower the robes with this mantra seven times before putting them on.
Homage to the Triple Gem.
Homage to the Tathāgata, the Holy Ocean of Wisdom, the All-Illuminating Adornment King.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Homage to the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Greatly Compassionate One.
Tadyathā: cuṭu cuṭu, he he he he, svāhā. World-Honored One, this is the mantra for incense and lamps.
If one enters the maṇḍala and wishes to offer incense,
one should first recite this mantra over the incense seven times before burning it.
When wishing to light lamps, one should first recite this mantra.
After reciting the mantra over the oil seven times, light the lamp.
Pay homage to the Triple Gem.
Pay homage to the Tathāgata Holy Ocean of Wisdom Universal Illumination Adornment King.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One.
Tadyathā: siri siri, idiri idiri, siri diri, svāhā. World-Honored One, this is the mantra for flowers, incense, and garlands.
If one enters the maṇḍala and wishes to make offerings of flowers, incense, and garlands,
one should first empower the flowers with this mantra seven times and scatter them over the honored image.
Furthermore, one should empower the incense with this mantra seven times and apply it to the honored image.
Furthermore, recite this mantra seven times over a flower garland to adorn the honored image.
Pay homage to the Triple Gem.
Pay homage to the Tathāgata Holy Ocean of Wisdom Universal Illumination Adornment King.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Homage to the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Greatly Compassionate One.
Tadyathā | sante sante | mṛte mṛte | sute sute | svāhā || O World-Honored One, this is the mantra for offering to the Buddha.
If one wishes to make offerings of food, drink, flowers, fruits, and so forth to the Buddha,
one should first recite this mantra twenty-one times over them before presenting them. Then,
pay homage to the Triple Gem.
Homage to the Tathāgata, the Holy Ocean of Wisdom, the All-Illuminating Adorned King.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Holy Avalokiteśvara, the Greatly Compassionate One.
Tadyathā | masi dasi | jarī jarī | huru huru | julu julu | suru suru | muru muru | svāhā | World-Honored One, this is the *kṣāra-mantra* (the mantra of caustic ash).
If one wishes to perform any ritual action using the aforementioned root mantra,
one should first consecrate *jāti* flowers with this mantra once before using them to kindle the fire.
Furthermore, separately take *jāti* flowers and wood,
cut them into thirty-one pieces each,
and soak them in curd, clarified butter, and honey overnight.
Each time one takes a section of the mantra,
recite it once and immediately cast it into the fire until all have been exhausted;
thereafter, perform whatever actions are required according to the specific purpose.
Homage to the Triple Gem.
Homage to the Tathāgata Āryajñānasāgaravirocanavyūharāja.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Homage to the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Greatly Compassionate One.
Tadyathā: 1. Āli mli 2. Vili ti 3. Jhi jhi hi 4. Svāhā. World-Honored One, this is the mantra for binding the boundary.
When one wishes to establish the boundary (sīmābandha),
first recite this mantra over water seven times and sprinkle it in the four directions;
alternatively, one may recite it over mustard seeds or pure ashes.
Recite this seven times for each of the four directions, extending as far as desired according to one's intention;
this shall establish the boundaries for protection.
Then, pay homage to the Triple Gem.
Homage to the Tathāgata, the Holy Ocean of Wisdom, the All-Illuminating Adornment King.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Holy Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One.

Tadyathā | biddhi biddhi | tiddhi tiddhi | jiddhi jiddhi | viddhi viddhi | gaccha gaccha | bhagavan | ārya avalokiteśvara | svabhāvasvabhāvena | svāhā || World-Honored One, this is the mantra for requesting [the Bodhisattva] to return to his own palace.
When the task you have undertaken is finished and you request that I return to my own palace,
you should recite this mantra over water seven times and sprinkle it in the four directions; I shall then return.
World-Honored One, although this divine mantra may not be established [by logical proof],
it is nonetheless capable of performing various activities;
if one recites it with a sincere heart, there is no wish that will not be fulfilled.
If one suffers from malaria that recurs once every day, or once every two days,
or once every three days, or once every four days;
or if one suffers from a demonic affliction caused by a bhūta spirit.
It may be caused by a *ḍākinī*, or caused by a *piśāca*,
or caused by a *kaṭapūtana*, or caused by a *graha* of epilepsy,
or caused by a *graha* of convulsions.
Or if it is caused by various other evil spirits,
one should recite this mantra over the patient one hundred and eight times,
and they will immediately be cured. If the obstruction is heavy, use five-colored thread and, while reciting the mantra, tie knots in it.
Tie one knot for each repetition, making a total of one hundred and eight knots.
Bind these around the neck or the arm of the patient to eliminate karmic hindrances.
It eliminates and heals diseases such as carbuncles, abscesses, fistulas, pustules, sores, ulcers, and scabies—
whatever various malignant ailments there may be—
as well as injuries from swords, arrows, spears, and lances.

If one is stung by snakes, scorpions, centipedes, venomous bees, or the like, recite this mantra over them seven times and they will immediately be healed. For those with heavy karmic obstructions, recite the mantra over yellow earth and mud up to seven sets of seven times (forty-nine times).
By applying it to the afflicted area, the suffering shall be eliminated and the ailment healed.
This applies to those suffering from flaccid paralysis (*śīta-vāta*),
hemiplegia (*pakṣāghāta*), convulsions (*apasmāra*), deafness, nasal congestion, or diseases caused by wind (*vāta*).
All should with a sincere heart recite this mantra one hundred and eight times for the patient; the illness will then be cured. If the karmic obstacles are heavy, use oil or clarified butter.
Fry birch bark and agarwood together, reciting the mantra seven times over them each time.
Then, apply it to the body, drip it into the ears or nose, or have the patient ingest it;
the ailment will be cured immediately. As for whatever other various diseases may remain, [the same method applies].
All should, with a sincere heart, recite this mantra for them;
or by reciting it oneself, one will immediately achieve recovery.
World-Honored One, if you wish to establish this divine mantra, [you should do so].
One should first fashion an image of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara out of high-quality, flawless white sandalwood,
measuring one and a half spans in length.
With his left hand he holds a red lotus *kamaṇḍalu*;
extending his right arm, he wears a rosary and makes the gesture of granting fearlessness (*abhaya-mudrā*).
The image has eleven faces.
The three faces in front display expressions of compassion;
the three faces on the left display expressions of wrath.
The three faces on the right side should be made with white fangs protruding upward;
the face directly behind should be made with a fierce, loud laughter;
and the face at the top of the head should be made in the likeness of a Buddha’s face.
Within each of the crowns, there is the form of a Buddha.
Upon the body of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
he is fully adorned with various ornaments such as necklaces and the like.
Once this image has been fashioned, those who wish to make a vow should don fresh,
clean garments and observe the fast and precepts from the first day of the waxing moon until the eighth day.
Recite this mantra three times each day,
one hundred and eight times or an immeasurable number of times.
Thereafter, in a quiet place, arrange a pure seat.
Place the crafted image of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva facing west.
Offer various foods and drinks according to your means,
burning only aloeswood and storax incense.
The practitioner should consume a diet of barley and milk.
Reciting as before until the thirteenth day, from this point forward,
the ritual offerings provided must be twice as superior as those previously arranged.
The practitioner should consume only the three white foods—
namely, milk, curd, and rice—
and kindle a fire before an image made of bodhi tree wood.
Furthermore, take that wood and cut it into one thousand and eight pieces.
Saturate them with *turuṣka* oil.
Taking each piece in turn, recite the mantra once for each.
They were cast into the fire until they were completely consumed;
at that time, the great earth trembled and shook violently,
and by this means, the body of the image also began to move.
From the mouth at the very top, a voice issued forth, praising the practitioner, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
You are able to seek and pray with such diligent perseverance."
I shall cause your aspirations to be fulfilled;
I shall cause you to soar through the air here,
or else I shall cause your movements to be unimpeded.
Alternatively, one may become a sovereign king among the rishis who maintain mantras,
or attain mastery and unimpeded power like my own.
Furthermore, the practitioner may, on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon, perform the practice.
Place an image of the Eleven-faced Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva within a stūpa containing the Buddha’s relics;
don new, clean robes and observe the fast and precepts.
Having fasted for one day and one night without drinking or eating,
take one thousand and eight *sumana* flowers.
For each flower taken, recite the mantra once.
They threw them onto the image until they were all exhausted;
at that time, the image faced forward,
and from its mouth there issued a sound like the roar of thunder.
Because of this, the great earth will tremble;
at that time, the practitioner should settle their own mind,
not give rise to fear, and simply recite the divine mantra.
When making a request for one’s aspiration, speak as follows:
"I pay homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Greatly Compassionate One.
At what time shall I be able to act as a great refuge for all sentient beings?"
He is able to fulfill all the heart's desires of sentient beings.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara grants their vows;
when he grants these vows, the devas, nāgas, and others—
There is no one who can create obstacles for them.
Furthermore, when there is a lunar eclipse,
the practitioner takes one *liang* of clarified butter and places it in a silver vessel.
Place this before the image and recite this mantra;
until the moon returns to its former state in this month,
take it as food, and all diseases within the body will be cured without exception.
Furthermore, the practitioner should take equal parts of realgar and ox-gall,
place them before this image, and recite this mantra one thousand and eight times.
Mix it with water and apply it to the space between the eyebrows.
The three accomplishments will be achieved as previously described.
If one bathes the body with this warm water, [the same results follow].
Then all obstacles, all evil dreams, and all epidemics shall be entirely cured and healed. Furthermore,
if enemies or bandits from other regions should wish to invade the borders, [this shall likewise prevail].
One should take a single pellet of *kajjala* (lamp-black) and,
having recited this mantra one hundred and eight times over it, use it to adorn this image.
On the left side, the wrathful face should be directed toward that direction.
This will cause the enemy's army to be unable to advance.
Furthermore, if an epidemic breaks out among the people or livestock within the kingdom,
one should burn *khadira* wood before this image.
Furthermore, take that wood separately and cut it into one thousand and eight pieces, each an inch long;
then take each piece and smear it with mustard oil.
Recite the mantra once and cast it into the fire until it is entirely consumed.
Then, take crimson thread and make seven knots while reciting the mantra;
with each recitation, tie one knot and fasten them upon the crown of the head of the foremost Buddha.
It can cause all pestilential diseases to be completely eliminated.
Once the pestilence has been removed, one should untie the mantra-cord.
Furthermore, if anyone should suddenly become possessed by *caṇḍa*-bhūtas, *piśācas*, or other such spirits and fall ill, [this rite shall be performed].
One should take white thread and make twenty-one mantra-knots,
reciting the mantra once for each knot.
Then, one should tie it around the crown of the head on the compassionate face positioned in front.
After staying for one night, it is removed and taken;
when tied around the patient's neck, the illness is immediately cured.
If the karmic obstacles are heavy and the illness is not cured, [the procedure is repeated].
One should take this cord and recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight more times. Then,
tie it to the crown of the head of the image previously bound,
and after one night has passed, untie and remove it.
If this is tied around the neck of a sick person, they will certainly be cured.
Furthermore, if there is a chronic illness that causes suffering and does not subside,
or if malevolent spirits and ghosts enter one's house;
One should take one hundred and eight pieces of frankincense (*guggulu*) and recite the mantra once over each piece before this image,
then cast them into the fire until they are all exhausted.
Furthermore, take white thread and make twenty-one mantra-knots,
tying one knot for each recitation.
Fasten it before you and place it upon the crown of the head of the face of Compassion.
After having remained for one night,
it is removed and tied around the neck of the patient;
thus the ailment is cured and the malevolent spirits are dispersed.
Furthermore, if one is pursued by enemies who seek an opportunity for harm,
or if they engage in strife, incantations, or prayers with the intent to cause ruin and injury,
one should make offerings of various kinds of incense, flowers, and other articles to this image.
Light a fire before an image made of *bhaṣaka* wood.
Take one hundred and eight seeds of *yūthikā*,
recite the mantra once over each, and cast them into the fire.
Furthermore, take white thread and tie one hundred and eight knots;
recite the mantra once for each knot and fasten it to the top of the wrathful face on the left side of this image.
After staying there for one night, he untied this rope,
called out the names of his enemies and rivals, and cut each individual knot, placing them in separate locations;
calling out one name and cutting one knot until they were all exhausted.
Now, whatever those enemies may have intended shall fail to be accomplished, and they will naturally submit.
Furthermore, if a person wishes to seek various auspicious and favorable matters,
they should take threads of five colors and tie them into a mantra-cord with one hundred and eight knots.
Recite the mantra once for each knot.
Furthermore, recite it seven times before the image,
then tie them and place them upon the crown of the compassionate face directly in front of you.
Having stayed for one night, one should untie it;
when tied upon one's own body, all that is sought will be as desired.
Furthermore, if one knows there are various obstacles or difficulties within the body, [one should proceed accordingly].
The virtuous matters one seeks often do not accord with one's wishes,
and misfortunes occasionally arrive without apparent cause;
one should bathe the body of this image with scented water.
Again, take this water and recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times;
use it to bathe the body of the image of Vināyaka.
Again, take [the water] and recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times, sprinkling it upon one's own body.
All obstacles and difficulties will naturally be extinguished,
and whatever one seeks shall not fail to accord with one's wishes.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, having spoken this sutra, [remained silent].
The entire great assembly simultaneously praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Great Being!
You have been able to proclaim this divine mantra for the sake of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings."
"We rejoice in this and also vow to uphold it.
At that time, the great assembly was filled with joy and leaped for gladness;
they circumambulated the Buddha three times, paid their respects, and departed.
The Eleven-Faced Divine Mantra Heart Sūtra
